Sourced from io.rest-assured:rest-assured's changelog.

Changelog 6.2.0 (2026-10-16)

Fix spring-web-test-client-kotlin-extensions bringing jakarta.servlet-api, jakarta.jakartaee-web-api and about 20 other Jakarta EE API jars to your classpath at runtime. They were declared with a scope that Maven doesn't know (optional), which it treated as a compile dependency, and are now provided, like in spring-mock-mvc-kotlin-extensions (#1992)

Upgraded scala-library in scala-support from 2.13.0 to 2.13.18, which fixes CVE-2022-36944, scala3-library_3 in scala-extensions from 3.3.3 to 3.3.8, Jackson 2 (jackson-databind, jackson-core and jackson-module-kotlin) from 2.17.1 to 2.22.3, Jackson 3 (tools.jackson) from 3.0.2 to 3.2.3, Gson from 2.9.0 to 2.14.0, Guava in json-schema-validator from 33.2.1-jre to 33.7.2-jre, commons-lang3 from 3.19.0 to 3.21.0, Yasson from 3.0.4 to 3.0.5 (now with its new group id org.eclipse.yasson, since org.eclipse:yasson 3.0.5 only relocates to it), Parsson from 1.1.7 to 1.1.9, Johnzon (johnzon-mapper) from 2.0.2 to 2.2.0 and jaxb-impl from 2.3.4 to 2.3.9 (#1986)

Non-backward compatible change: sending a request directly from a request specification created by RequestSpecBuilder.build() (for example spec.when().get("/x") or spec.post()) now fails with an IllegalStateException that tells you to use given().spec(spec) or given(spec), instead of a NullPointerException. then(), expect() and response() on such a specification also throw this exception, where they returned null before. The specification is meant to be added to a request, and isn't changed by the failed call. The javadoc of RequestSpecBuilder.build() now explains this (part of #1863)

Non-backward compatible change: sending a request directly from a response specification created by ResponseSpecBuilder.build() (for example responseSpec.when().get("/x")) now fails with an IllegalStateException that tells you to use given().spec(requestSpec).expect().spec(responseSpec), then().spec(responseSpec) or given(requestSpec, responseSpec), instead of a NullPointerException. when(), given(), with() and request() on such a specification also throw this exception, where they returned null before. Using the specification in a request, or as RestAssured.responseSpecification, works as before. The javadoc of ResponseSpecBuilder.build() now explains this (related to #1863)

JsonPath and JSON body assertions can now read a key that contains a colon with the dot notation, such as jsonPath.getInt("message.ErrorCode:") or body("message.ErrorCode:", equalTo(0)), which failed with "Invalid JSON expression" before. A colon in a ternary (a ? b : c) or Elvis (a ?: b) expression, in a closure or in a quoted string is left as is (fixes #1766)

Fix request logging of a multipart File whose mime type isn't text, such as application/octet-stream (the default) or image/png, which since 5.5.0 printed the whole file content to the log. Such a part is now logged as the path of the file, as before 5.5.0. The content of a file with a text mime type (text/*, JSON, XML or HTML) is still logged, and is now read with the charset of the part (or of its mime type), or UTF-8 if none is given, instead of the platform default charset. A text file that can't be read is logged as its path, so sending the request reports the error (fixes #1819)

Upgraded Groovy from 5.0.3 to 5.0.8 and Apache HttpClient (httpclient and httpmime) from 4.5.13 to 4.5.14 (#1971)

Fix races in the static configuration of REST Assured when tests run in parallel. RestAssured.filters(..), replaceFiltersWith(..), registerParser(..) and unregisterParser(..), and RestAssuredMockMvc.resultHandlers(..) and postProcessors(..), could make a given() in another thread fail with a ConcurrentModificationException or copy a default filter list with missing or null filters. given() (and when(), with(), expect() and the static request methods) no longer changes any shared state. The public static fields of RestAssured, RestAssuredMockMvc and RestAssuredWebTestClient, and JsonPath.config, XmlPath.config and JsonSchemaValidator.settings, are now volatile, so a value set before the tests start is seen by every thread. The javadoc of RestAssured, RestAssuredMockMvc and RestAssuredWebTestClient now explains how to use the static configuration when tests run in parallel (fixes #1967)

Non-backward compatible change: given() no longer writes the session id into the RestAssured.config field or RestAssured.defaultParser into the global parser registry. While RestAssured.sessionId is set, RestAssured.config() returns the config with the session id, but the RestAssured.config field doesn't contain it, also not after a request, so given().config(RestAssured.config) no longer sends the static session id (use RestAssured.config() instead). Setting RestAssured.sessionId or RestAssured.defaultParser back to null now takes effect without RestAssured.reset(). A list returned by RestAssured.filters() before replaceFiltersWith(..) keeps showing the old filters (fixes #1967)

Fix HttpClientConfig.reuseHttpClientInstance() creating more than one HttpClient when several threads send their first request at the same time, and make the default Yasson (JSON-B) object mapper share one Jsonb instance between threads in the same way. Note that the reused HttpClient is reconfigured by every request, so it still must not be used by requests that run at the same time (fixes #1967)

Non-backward compatible change: auth().certificate(certURL, password) and RestAssured.certificate(certURL, password), with or without CertificateAuthSettings, now use the file at certURL as key store, as documented, so the client certificate in it is sent to servers that ask for one (mutual TLS). Before, the file was only used as trust store, which it still is. This means that a private key in the file is now offered to any server that asks for a client certificate, also where it's optional (such as nginx with ssl_verify_client optional), which may then reject a certificate it doesn't trust, and that the private key must have the password of the file. To avoid this, or to use the JVM's default trust store, use RestAssured.certificate(trustStorePath, trustStorePassword, keyStorePath, keyStorePassword, CertificateAuthSettings) (as RestAssured.authentication or with RequestSpecBuilder.setAuth(..)), where an empty path means no key store or the default trust store (fixes #1158, related to #1325)

Fix a root path with more than one placeholder left for a later withArgs(..), such as rootPath("a.%s.%s.%s", withArgs("x")).body(withArgs("y", "z"), ..), which failed with a MissingFormatArgumentException. All placeholders without an argument, including ones such as %d, are now kept for later arguments. body(withArgs(..), matcher) also no longer adds a trailing dot to the path, which showed up in failure messages such as "JSON path a.d.e. doesn't match." (fixes #1949)

The rest-assured module is now written entirely in Java and no longer depends on Groovy (org.apache.groovy:groovy and groovy-xml) directly. Groovy still comes transitively through json-path and xml-path, which use it for GPath, so the dependencies on the classpath are unchanged. The rest-assured and rest-assured-common OSGi bundles no longer import the groovy packages, and rest-assured-common no longer depends on Groovy at all (#1917, #1932)

Non-backward compatible change: a Groovy closure used as request body now fails with an IllegalArgumentException. This could only happen when a custom ObjectMapper returned a Closure from serialize(..), in which case the closure was run as a builder (a JsonBuilder for JSON, a StreamingMarkupBuilder for XML and HTML, or with a Writer or OutputStream for text and binary content). Return a String, byte[] or InputStream from the ObjectMapper instead (#1914)

Non-backward compatible change: a request body that isn't a String (for example a byte[], InputStream or File) sent with content-type application/x-www-form-urlencoded now fails with an IllegalArgumentException explaining that a form url-encoded body must be a String, instead of a groovy.lang.MissingMethodException (#1914)

Non-backward compatible change: a groovy.lang.Writable request body sent with a text content-type is now sent as its toString() instead of what its writeTo(..) method writes. Groovy's own Writables (such as JsonBuilder and GString) produce the same output either way. A Groovy WritableFile (file.asWritable()) is now sent like any other File, read with the charset of the request content-type (#1914)

Fix the failure message of a body path assertion when the response body can't be parsed into something the path can navigate (for example a JSON body that is just a string), which showed the literal text $contentParser instead of the response body (#1922)

Fix form authentication failing with "IllegalArgumentException: parameterValues cannot be null" when an additional input field given to FormAuthConfig.withAdditionalField(s)(..) is an input tag without a value attribute on the login page. The field is now sent as a form parameter without a value (#1921)

Fix matchesDtd(URL) in RestAssuredMatchers, RestAssuredMockMvcMatchers and RestAssuredWebTestClientMatchers, which always failed with a GroovyCastException ("Cannot cast object '' with class 'java.lang.String' to class 'java.io.InputStream'") when the response was validated. The DTD is now read from the URL, every time the matcher is used (#1920)

Non-backward compatible change: matchesXsdInClasspath(..) and matchesDtdInClasspath(..) (in RestAssuredMatchers, RestAssuredMockMvcMatchers and RestAssuredWebTestClientMatchers) now fail with an IllegalArgumentException saying that the XSD or DTD couldn't be found in classpath, instead of a groovy.lang.GroovyRuntimeException ("Ambiguous method overloading"). The XSD and DTD matchers now also fail with an IllegalArgumentException when asked to match something that isn't a String, for example body("some.path", matchesXsd(..)) where the path returns an element that has child elements, instead of a Groovy exception (#1920)

Non-backward compatible change: io.restassured.assertion.HeaderMatcher, DetailedCookieAssertion, ResponseTimeMatcher and StreamVerifier are now written in Java and no longer implement groovy.lang.GroovyObject. HeaderMatcher.validateHeader(..), DetailedCookieAssertion.validateCookies(..) and ResponseTimeMatcher.validate(..) now return Map instead of Object, HeaderMatcher.validateHeader(..) takes a Response, and HeaderMatcher.getMatcher() and get/setResponseAwareMatcher(..) are now generically typed (Matcher and ResponseAwareMatcher) (#1919)

A header expectation whose header name is neither a String nor a GString (for example an Integer key in the map passed to headers(Map)) now checks the header named by the key's string form instead of failing with a groovy.lang.MissingMethodException (#1919)

Non-backward compatible change: io.restassured.internal.http.HTTPBuilder, which a custom AuthenticationScheme receives in authenticate(..), no longer uses Groovy closures. Its get(..) methods, the request(..) overloads that took a Closure, getHandler() and the post(..) and patch(..) overloads without a response handler are removed. post(..), patch(..) and request(..) now take an HttpResponseHandler or a RequestConfigurer, and response handlers always take two arguments (the response and its parsed content) (#1923)

A parameter name that is neither a String nor a GString (for example an Integer key in the map passed to params(Map), queryParams(Map), formParams(Map) or pathParams(Map)) is now used in its string form, so 1 becomes "1", instead of failing with a groovy.lang.MissingMethodException (#1927)

Non-backward compatible change: io.restassured.internal.RestAssuredResponseOptionsGroovyImpl is removed and its logic now lives in RestAssuredResponseOptionsImpl, so getGroovyResponse(), setGroovyResponse(..) and the protected groovyResponse field of RestAssuredResponseOptionsImpl
